steps.title: Passing and storing functions as values

blocks.text: Defining a function creates a function object bound to its name. The bare name refers to that function; name(arguments) calls it.
Pass a function itself when the receiving helper requires a function object.
You can store a callable and invoke it later.
A helper can call its supplied function parameter with parameter(value). Passing an earlier call’s result is different from supplying the function.

blocks.text: A nested function can resolve a free name in an enclosing function scope. Each call has its own local bindings.
A returned nested function can still use enclosing values after the call that created it has finished.
Use nonlocal name to rebind an existing name in the nearest enclosing function scope.
A stateful factory can bind state and return a nested function that reads it and uses nonlocal to rebind it.

blocks.code:
def make_counter():
    count = 0
    def advance():
        nonlocal count
        count = count + 1
        return count
    return advance

counter = make_counter()
print(counter())
print(counter())
other = make_counter()
print(other())

annotations.text: State belongs to this factory call.
The returned function retains access to enclosing state.
First factory call: retain its own binding.
Separate factory call: distinct local state.
The separate other counter starts at 1.

segments.label: Read an enclosing binding and update it with nonlocal
segments.summary: An outer function binds a variable to 10 and calls an inner function that reads that enclosing value. Adding an ordinary assignment inside the inner function creates a local binding instead: the inner function reports 20, while the outer function still reports 10. Declaring the name nonlocal before assigning redirects the update to the existing enclosing binding, so both functions report 20.

bridge.before: Watch how reading an enclosing name differs from assigning to it. Compare the inner and outer values before and after the nonlocal declaration.
bridge.after: The clip demonstrates enclosing-name access and rebinding, but not independent factory calls or retained state after return. The text covers those behaviors with a counter factory.

public.prompt: Choose the independently created closure so counter and other retain separate state. Change only the final counter assignment so counter uses the independent closure rather than sharing other. The checker calls counter twice and other once; their results must be 1, 2, and 1.

files.content:
initial_count = 0
if True:

    def make_counter():
        count = initial_count

        def advance():
            nonlocal count
            count = count + 1
            return count
        return advance
independent_counter = make_counter()
other = make_counter()
counter = other
